deletion_policy.Description:
The deletion policy for the user. Setting ABANDON allows the resource
				to be abandoned rather than deleted. This is useful for Postgres, where users cannot be deleted from the API if they
				have been granted SQL roles. Possible values are: "ABANDON".

host.Description: The host the user can connect from. This is only supported for MySQL instances. Don't set this field for PostgreSQL instances. Can be an IP address. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

instance.Description: The name of the Cloud SQL instance. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

name.Description: The name of the user. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.

password.Description:
The password for the user. Can be updated. For Postgres instances this is a Required field, unless type is set to
                either CLOUD_IAM_USER or CLOUD_IAM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT.

allowed_failed_attempts.Description: Number of failed attempts allowed before the user get locked.

enable_failed_attempts_check.Description: If true, the check that will lock user after too many failed login attempts will be enabled.

enable_password_verification.Description: If true, the user must specify the current password before changing the password. This flag is supported only for MySQL.

password_expiration_duration.Description: Password expiration duration with one week grace period.

locked.Description: If true, user does not have login privileges.

password_expiration_time.Description: Password expiration duration with one week grace period.

project.Description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

disabled.Description: If the user has been disabled.

server_roles.Description: The server roles for this user in the database.

type.Description:
The user type. It determines the method to authenticate the user during login.
                The default is the database's built-in user type. Flags include "BUILT_IN", "CLOUD_IAM_USER", "CLOUD_IAM_GROUP" or "CLOUD_IAM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT".
